title: Gigantes Yahni
subtitle: Greek giant butter beans braised slowly in tomato and olive oil
excerpt: Large butter beans simmered in a rich tomato and herb sauce until very tender and creamy inside. A Greek taverna staple that improves overnight and needs nothing but bread alongside.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek meze dish; oven-braised version common in home kitchens across Greece.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the sauce. Thaw overnight and reheat gently on the hob with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the recipe with no changes to timing. Use a wide, deep baking dish.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best made a day ahead. The beans absorb the sauce overnight and the flavour deepens.

content.text: Gigantes yahni are large white beans cooked low and slow in olive oil and tomato. The beans must be fully soft before going into the oven or they will stay firm in the middle. Use a generous amount of olive oil as it is the foundation of the sauce.
Heat the oven to 180C. Heat half the olive oil in a wide frying pan over a medium heat. Cook the onions for 10 minutes until soft and starting to colour.
Add the garlic, tomato puree and oregano. Cook for 2 minutes, stirring often.
Add the tinned tomatoes, vegetable stock and bay leaves. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Tip the drained beans into a wide roasting tin or deep baking dish. Pour the tomato sauce over them. Stir gently to combine.
Drizzle the remaining olive oil over the top. Cover tightly with foil and bake for 60 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for a further 30 minutes until the sauce thickens and the top begins to colour.
Remove the bay leaves. Scatter over the parsley and serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The beans are still firm after 90 minutes.
items.cause: Tinned beans vary in their softness. Some brands hold their shape longer.
items.fix: Re-cover with foil, add a splash more stock and return to the oven for 20 minutes.

items.symptom: The sauce dries out and catches.
items.cause: The foil was not sealed well or the oven runs hot.
items.fix: Check at 45 minutes. Add water or stock if the dish looks dry before returning to the oven.

items.cause: Not enough salt, or too little olive oil.
items.fix: Add more salt at the end and finish with a generous drizzle of extra-virgin olive oil before serving.
